note: The eight exhibits below are compiled specimens, not captures of named third-party repositories: NECROPSY cannot verify a live repository's numbers offline, and printing unverified counts under a real project's name would be a fabrication (P7). Each specimen exhibits one failure mode from design.md section 8.4 and exercises the real pipeline. To build a wall of real repositories, replace these entries with the ones you want and run `seed-graveyard --refresh` with a GITHUB_TOKEN set; that rewrites each fixture from the API and sets fixture_provenance to api_verified.

entries.curator_note: The clearest death there is: the owner archived it and said why in the README. Archived status floors the abandonment factor at 0.85, so this exhibit shows what that floor does to a score.
entries.why_it_is_a_good_exhibit: The clearest death there is: the owner archived it and said why in the README.
entries.failure_mode: archived by owner with a farewell README

entries.curator_note: Pinned to a framework release that went out of support before the final commit. The dependency-rot factor carries this exhibit, and every flagged package is named by the offline deprecation table.
entries.why_it_is_a_good_exhibit: Pinned to a framework release that went out of support before the final commit.
entries.failure_mode: dependency-era death: framework major version reached EOL

entries.curator_note: Healthy code, absent maintainer. Twenty-eight of the thirty sampled issues have no reply. Described structurally, never personally: the finding is the sample, not the person (P6).
The author said it was unfinished and was telling the truth. Small, licensed, no tests. Low difficulty is the right answer here, and it is a different diagnosis from abandonment.
entries.why_it_is_a_good_exhibit: The author said it was unfinished and was telling the truth.
entries.failure_mode: declared work-in-progress, never finished, tiny codebase

entries.curator_note: The counter-example the wall needs. Tests, CI, a licence, documentation, a changelog, and no commit in four years. Stale is not the same as rotten, and the score says so.
Nothing legally reusable, nothing that proves it works, nothing that runs. Three of the eight factors sit at 1.0, which is what a legal and verification vacuum looks like on the scorecard.
entries.why_it_is_a_good_exhibit: Nothing legally reusable, nothing that proves it works, nothing that runs.
entries.failure_mode: no licence, no tests, no CI, moderate size

entries.curator_note: Finished is a diagnosis, not an insult (P6). Complete tests, modern CI, an OSI licence, real documentation, a lockfile, no deprecated dependencies, and no reason to commit again. It is genuinely dead and genuinely easy to pick up, which is what the lowest band is for.
entries.why_it_is_a_good_exhibit: Finished is a diagnosis, not an insult (P6).
entries.failure_mode: successful but finished: dead, and legitimately cheap to revive

entries.curator_note: Four thousand files, two frameworks halfway swapped, and a branch note where the migration stopped. The top of the scale exists for this shape of repository.
entries.why_it_is_a_good_exhibit: Four thousand files, two frameworks halfway swapped, and a branch note where the migration stopped.
entries.failure_mode: huge abandoned monolith, abandoned during a migration
